sourceInformation.source: Astro Battle Space Invaders - 1979. Interpreted as Bally's Astrocade Space Invaders, later Astro Battle; the renamed manual bears a 1981 copyright. This interpretation is not a new release-history finding.
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.89.1, commit 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691; native Canvas2D; JavaScript; Web Audio; AI Hub session client 1.4.0 / Protocol v1, commit 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869. Self-contained HTML; no CDN or runtime downloads.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded retro-modern pixel art using native sprites, hue-shifted ramps, stepped planet lighting and three location palettes.
sourceInformation.animation: Native E.anim, game.tween and engine fixed clocks; procedural recoil, beat-synchronized march poses, shell breaks, repair clusters, debris and flagship opening/closing states.
sourceInformation.audio: Runtime oscillator/noise synthesis through native music, SFX and voice buses; original location loops, march pulse, result stingers and synthesized gibberish barks. Music defaults and resets to 10%. No audio files.
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo and simultaneous local two-player co-op. AI Hub supplies online one- or two-seat shared-world co-op with host authority, complete reliable snapshots, input heartbeats and server-only hosting. No standalone remote matchmaking.
sourceInformation.testing: 133 automated checks: deterministic simulation, complete ordinary-action standard solo and co-op campaigns, ordinary solo and local co-op campaigns through the native exported scripts, headless draw/UI, Chromium input/audio, standard gamepad stubs, phone/tablet emulation, Firefox/WebKit startup/input smoke, isolated file export, and the pinned Hub harness plus semantic state checks. Hub scenarios use 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter and 5% loss. Physical controller feel, human listening, real TV distance, physical iOS behavior and novice first-run duration are unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Read Bally Alley's HTML manual and inspected pages of the five-page manual scan. Inspected the October 1982 comparison scan, especially printed page 66, and eight extracted frames from the linked Nice and Games Astro Battle review around 80-96 seconds. Confirmed colored rows, marching poses, four arched bunkers and erosion visually. Historical audio listening is unknown. New co-op, repairs, specialists and hostile flagship are original design additions.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux; Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS on WSL2. Installed Node 24.21.0 and Python Playwright 1.63.0.

testingFeedback: 15 distinct issues across automated checks, visual inspection and implementation review; all fixed. The issue log records root causes, severity and the check that caught each one.
1 critical issue: at an exact bunker-cell boundary, repeated shots could hit a neighboring cell that erosion never removed. Swept hits now erode the actual collided cell, with a regression test.

The lossy Hub semantic fire-and-repair check. It exposed the boundary collision bug even though complete ordinary campaign bots and transport conformance passed; it also verifies remote masks, repair cost, deaths, protected respawns and terminal agreement.
The initial boot-only smoke check. It confirmed startup and native drawing but could not establish ordinary playability or remote world agreement.
engineFeedback: Native sprite, palette, animation, synthesis and exact headless stepping fit a self-contained arcade cartridge well.

Yes: sampling only held input missed quick mouse repair clicks, and mixing pointer-down actions with native compatibility clicks advanced menus twice. One action route and pressed-edge sampling fixed these. The documented arcade helper alternates players, so simultaneous co-op uses a shared simulation.
The serializable shared-world simulation, destructible bunker masks and aperture-preserving repair rules.
Keeping engine input ownership, local overlays and the Hub clock separate while preserving one combat rectangle on portrait and landscape displays.
none; the full pinned engine is embedded unchanged. Game adapters supply simultaneous co-op, swept collision, custom controller-first pages and session authority.
A native serializable fixed-screen co-op example with swept projectile collision and an explicit session clock adapter.
promptFeedback: The source research, finite campaign, two-action constraint and concrete completion tests gave the game a clear identity.
The source name was ambiguous; the plan's explicit Astrocade interpretation resolved it. The engine's default alternating co-op also needed to be distinguished from simultaneous play.
Making destructive cover, ordinary-input full campaign completion and authoritative lossy-network co-op agree on the same rules.
Keep the detailed acceptance contracts, but provide the pinned engine and matching Hub harness as an attached package to reduce setup ambiguity.

aiHub.name: Astro Battle Jam
aiHub.tagline: Cut a lane. Patch the planet.
aiHub.description: A colorful planetary-defense shooter where your own missiles carve firing lanes through cover and alien salvage rebuilds it. Defend three locations through six formations and a two-phase flagship, solo, in local co-op or together through AI Hub.
aiHub.controls: Move: stick/D-pad, A/D or arrows, mouse target; fire: R2/Cross, Space or left click; repair: L1/Square, Q or right click; Options/Esc pauses. Touch: drag, assisted fire, second finger cuts cover, contextual repair.
